Erik Ninn-Hansen (1922-2014) was a Danish Conservative politician who had a long and ultimately controversial political career.

## Political Career
- Served as a member of the Danish Parliament (Folketing) from 1964 to 1994
- Held several ministerial positions, including Minister of Justice (1989-1993)
- Was known as a prominent figure in the Conservative People's Party

## The Tamil Case Scandal
Ninn-Hansen became most famous for his role in the "Tamil Case" (Tamilsagen), one of Denmark's biggest political scandals:
- As Justice Minister, he was found to have illegally delayed family reunification applications for Tamil refugees from Sri Lanka in 1987-1989
- The delays violated Danish law and separated Tamil families for extended periods
- In 1993, he was impeached by the Danish Parliament in a rare Court of Impeachment proceeding
- In 1995, he was convicted and received a four-month suspended prison sentence
- This was only the fifth impeachment trial in Danish history and the first resulting in conviction since 1910

## Aftermath
- Resigned as Justice Minister in 1993
- Left Parliament in 1994
- The scandal significantly damaged the Conservative People's Party's reputation
- The case led to important discussions about ministerial responsibility and the rule of law in Denmark

Ninn-Hansen passed away in 2014 at age 92. Despite his long political service, his legacy remains largely defined by the Tamil Case scandal.
